_doc: NextHack bank manifest -- the single place that says WHICH BANK each module's
code and consts live in, for both targets.
The build (build.ps1 / build-zx128.ps1) turns each entry into zcc's
--codeseg/--constseg flags, so moving a module between banks is ONE edit here:
no source change, and only the modules whose assignment changed recompile.
The sources therefore carry NO '#pragma codeseg/constseg' -- an in-file pragma
silently OVERRIDES the command line (verified), so re-adding one takes a module
A module with no 'code'/'const' key is RESIDENT (0x8000-0xBFF0): its code, and
its string/const literals, cost resident bytes. 'code' alone banks the code but
leaves the literals resident; adding 'const' banks the literals too (the
reclaim lever -- see the bank-budget skill).
Every module in the target's build list must appear here (the build refuses an
undeclared one), and the 'colocate' groups are checked before compiling.
Run 'python tools/bankmap.py' to see what each bank has left.

next._doc: Next: banks 10/11/13/14 as PAGE_20/22/26/28_CODE (ORG'd in mmap.inc); BANK_16..21 are z88dk-predefined sections holding the Layer 2 images.
next._pool_doc: The banks tools/bankpack.py may pack into. NOT PAGE_24_CODE (bank 12) -- that is PAGE_22's const spill, and a section ORG'd there collides. A module assigned to a bank outside this pool is PINNED: BANK_16..21 are read in place by the Layer 2 hardware. To add a bank: a SECTION + ORG in mmap.inc, then list it here (bank 15 is now nexthack_lvl's; 22+ are still free).

mainentry.why: resident: main() -- the CRT jumps straight to it, so it cannot be banked

platform.why: resident: the per-cell draw primitives + keyboard, called from every bank

rng.why: resident: rn2 is a hot leaf

nexthack_lvl.why: the cold level half split out of nexthack.c: build_level, the altar/fountain/pet/follower placement and the stairs. Deliberately NOT in nexthack.c's bank -- the point of the split was to get these bytes out of the classes+spells colocate group. In its own bank 15 rather than PAGE_20, which it would have squeezed to 344 B: the Next has spare banks, so the split buys headroom instead of moving the shortage

nexthack.why: the game core; const banks every message/label literal next to the code that prints it

classes.why: shares nexthack.c's bank on purpose -- draw_status/show_help read its tables in place

spells.why: shares nexthack.c's bank like classes.c; spell names/messages cost zero resident bytes

titlepal.why: GENERATED. Must sit in the bank show_layer2() runs from -- it streams this palette with that bank mapped

sfx.why: beeper effects; its literals stay resident (there are none worth banking)

platform_init.why: one-time init runs from any bank; const holds the ~3 KB gfx[] tile table next to load_gfx_tiles(), its only reader. Moved off PAGE_22 when the mines tiles + conduct code overflowed it

monster_spawn.why: split out of monster_ai.c when the AI banks filled up

music.why: the AY title theme + its score tables

monster_ai.why: bank 13, a third code bank opened when PAGE_20 filled up

leveltmpl.why: const holds the generated leveltmpl_data.h grids; load_template() reads them in place, so both must share a bank. Moved off PAGE_26 with the 128K half, so monster_ai + levelfov get that bank to themselves

levelfov.why: moved off PAGE_20 when bank 10 filled up as item.c grew

item.why: bank 14, item.c's own bank: the v0.9 reclaim banked the whole object catalogue with it, ~3.2 KB off the resident half

titlegfx0.why: GENERATED. Layer 2 reads this third of the title image IN PLACE from bank 16 -- hardware-pinned, never repack

zx128._doc: 128K: only banks 0/1/3/4/6/7 are pageable at 0xC000 (2 and 5 are fixed; 7 is free only because the shadow screen is never used). Six banks = a HARD 96 KB ceiling for banked code. ORG'd in zpragma-zx128.inc; each bank is also a tape-loader block in tools/mktap128.py.
zx128._contended_doc: The ULA steals cycles from the odd banks, so code there runs slower. It is a PREFERENCE, not a rule: a module marked "hot" (per-turn code) is placed in an uncontended bank when one has room, and nexthack itself already sits in the contended BANK_3 because its colocate group has nowhere else to go. The Next has no such split, so it declares none.
zx128._pool_doc: Every bank this machine has. There is no seventh: 2 holds the resident half and 5 is the always-mapped data bank. Adding one is impossible, so a plan that does not fit here is a real budget wall, not a placement accident.

mainentry.why: resident: main() -- the CRT jumps straight to it, so it cannot be banked

platform.why: resident: the per-cell ULA blits + keyboard, called from every bank

rng.why: resident: rn2 is a hot leaf

item.why: item.c's own bank (the v0.9 reclaim) -- the 128K's spare uncontended bank

monster_spawn.why: split out of monster_ai.c when BANK_6 filled up

sfx.why: moved BACK here from BANK_3 when the 0.12 batch (farlook + mirroring + traps) filled BANK_3. All sfx_* entries are __banked and bit_beepfx + its tables are resident, so the move costs nothing

nexthack_lvl.why: the cold level half split out of nexthack.c (see the Next entry). BANK_7 because it had ~14 KB free and this code runs once per level entry, so its contended RAM costs nothing

nexthack.why: the game core; const banks every message/label literal next to the code that prints it

classes.why: shares nexthack.c's bank on purpose -- draw_status/show_help read its tables in place

scr.why: the SCR blitter; must share a bank with the two screens below, which it reads in place

title_scr.why: GENERATED. The 6912-byte title SCR, read in place by scr.c

victory_scr.why: GENERATED. The 6912-byte victory SCR, read in place by scr.c

levelfov.why: moved out of BANK_1 when item.c's growth filled it; BANK_4 held the SCR screens with room to spare

monster_ai.why: the spare bank -- the pet AI outgrew BANK_1

leveltmpl.why: const holds the generated template grids, read in place by load_template(). Moved off BANK_6 (2026-08-31) to leave that uncontended bank to monster_ai alone: this module is read ONCE on entering a template level, so BANK_7's contended RAM costs it nothing, while the per-turn AI would feel it. Earlier it shared BANK_3 with nexthack.c; as that code grew the combined section silently overflowed 16 KB and the truncated template data crashed every template level -- mktap128.py now refuses an oversized bank

platform_init.why: moved here when BANK_3 overflowed. It runs ONCE at boot, so bank 7's contended RAM costs nothing, and its only const (udg_src) is read solely by build_udgs in the same file. NOTE udg_ink, which the renderers read everywhere, lives in the resident platform.c

music.why: the AY title theme + its score tables; bank 7 has ~14 KB free

colocate.why: classes.c/spells.c hand their const tables and literals to nexthack.c's code (draw_status, show_help, the class picker). A pointer into a bank that is NOT mapped reads garbage, so these three must share one bank.
show_layer2() (in nexthack.c) streams these palettes to NextReg 0x44 while its OWN bank is mapped in, so each palette must live in that same bank. Next only.
scr.c copies these SCRs to the ULA screen by dereferencing them directly, so the data must live in the bank scr.c runs from. 128K only.
